text:
rebecca-cs: Quick triage - customer 'QuillPay' onboarding: after enabling both server API key (long-lived) for backend calls and ephemeral tokens for mobile, they started seeing a mix of 401s and 429s. They rolled out a hotfix and now we see spikes in the rate window tied to the server key.

owen-platform: Can you paste a short log sample+SDK versions? Also confirm whether web + mobile both call the same endpoints.

rebecca-cs: SDKs: android 1.4.2, ios 1.4.2, web-js 0.9.0. Log snippet from their backend gateway that proxies mobile token requests:

```
INFO auth: issuing ephemeral token userId=abc123
WARN frontend: POST /v1/complete 401 missing auth
INFO auth: received server-key request from CI (key=sk-prod-xxxxx)
ERROR gateway: POST /v1/complete 429 quota_exceeded window=60s attribution=sk-prod-xxxxx
```

They accidentally used the production server key from CI for some automated test clients which hammered generate endpoints during rollout. Mobile ephemeral tokens were fine but the server key burst consumed the rate window and produced 429s for everyone.

felix-eng: Two separate problems: (A) mixed credentials causing surprising attribution and quota exhaustion, (B) clients retrying aggressively on 401 and replaying to same key. Quick recommendations: (1) rotate the CI server key immediately and mark it for non-production use, (2) reduce retry amplification by doing refresh+single-replay instead of aggressive loop, (3) add per-request Authorization injection (interceptor/adapter) so pooled connections don't leak stale headers, (4) for onboarding, recommend using a scoped limited key for tests.

sara-support: KB we send: gate token issuance, ensure backends don't proxy production sk for automated tests; example env guard: `if (ENV == "ci") use TEST_KEY` and pseudo-config for SDKs to set preflight coalesce. Example Android snippet:

```
// Android: serialized init + interceptor
AtomicBoolean inited = new AtomicBoolean(false);
if (inited.compareAndSet(false,true)) {
  String tok = fetchTokenBlocking();
  Thread.sleep(ThreadLocalRandom.current().nextInt(200, 800));
  RedwoodSdk.init(context, new SdkConfig.Builder()
    .preflightCoalesce(true)
    .maxPreflightConcurrency(3)
    .build(), tok);
  inited.set(false);
}
// OkHttp interceptor: add Authorization header per request from token cache
```

felix-eng: Server-side short-term mitigations: (a) add a five-second leaky-cache for ephemeral tokens returned to mobile to smooth spikes, (b) detect and throttle suspicious server-key traffic (CI) by IP or tag, (c) temporarily increase the quota window for this customer if business-critical while they fix key usage. Also add a rule in onboarding playbook: never expose prod sk to test harnesses.

rebecca-cs: I advised QuillPay to rotate the leaked server key, rollback the CI job that used it, and apply single-init + jitter on mobile. They also reduced client retry aggressiveness.

deploy-bot: [alert] edge.rate.quillpay.prod spike -> 429s increased by 470% in the last 5m. Tagging @owen-platform

owen-platform: Watching dashboards. If the server key rotation doesn't clear the spike in ~10m we should escalate to infra to apply temporary quota bump. Also we should capture this as a new onboarding checklist item: "segregate test vs prod keys + CI gating."

sara-support: I'll send the KB + a short one-pager about credential hygiene and retry playbook. Also adding a note to the onboarding repo.

rebecca-cs: Customer confirmed: rotating CI key + adding single-init and jitter reduced 429s to baseline. We'll keep the ticket open a bit to ensure no regression, then close and add playbook entry.
